Issued at 138 AM MST Sat Nov 14 2026

Above normal temperatures and mostly quiet weather will prevail 
across much of the Cowboy State this weekend. For Saturday a nearing 
trough will try to bring some precipitation chances to portions of 
southern and western WY. However, due to it being so unorganized and 
the bulk of the energy tracking farther south, much of the state 
will remain dry. A few rain/snow showers cannot be ruled out this 
morning into the early afternoon hours today. The best chances 30-
60% will be across far southwestern and western WY with lesser 
chances elsewhere. The higher elevations of western WY may see a 
very light coating of snow but overall accumulations will be little 
to non existent. Locations east of the Divide will remain dry with 
breaks in the cloud cover by the afternoon likely allowing for 
sunshine to break through. Temperatures will be in the mid to upper 
50s east of the Divide and mid to upper 40s west of the Divide. 
Sunday is looking quite nice with clouds decreasing allowing for 
plenty of sunshine throughout the day. Temperatures are expected to 
remain around the same values as Saturday. Winds do look to increase 
across the Wind Corridor by the afternoon from Rock Springs to 
Casper. Speeds of 15 to 25 mph with gusts of 30 to 40 mph will be 
likely during the afternoon. 

The start of the work week will see pleasant, dry, and mild 
conditions continue across the region. Temperatures will be similar 
to Sunday with breezy winds once again expected in the afternoon 
from Casper to Rock Springs. Another disturbance looks to be on the 
horizon for late Tuesday afternoon into Wednesday. This disturbance 
is in association with a trough that digs across the western CONUS 
starting late Monday. However, energy with this trough is likely to 
struggle to organize as it tracks east throughout the day Tuesday. 
Models do not really show any well defined closed low developing 
which will limit impacts. Precipitation chances overall do look much 
better than this most recent system, especially for the higher 
elevation mountains and western WY. Along with better precipitation 
chances this disturbance will bring cooler and seasonable 
temperatures to the area.

The current forecast is for showers to move into western WY late 
Tuesday behind a cold front that will gradually sweep west to east 
over the region. Temperatures may be a little too warm for snow to 
initially fall for the western valleys but they should cool quite 
quickly allowing for a transition over to snow. Snow showers will be 
possible through the overnight Tuesday into Wednesday across 
portions of western and southern WY. Some precipitation may make it 
across the Divide but dynamics may not be the most favorable. So at 
this time the best chances for precipitation will remain over 
western and southern WY along with the higher elevation mountains of 
western, central, and northern WY. Winds are another aspect to 
monitor as initially models showed a potent area of 700 mb winds 
move over central WY. However, the recent trends have lowered these 
winds, that being said some gusty winds of 30 to 40 mph still look 
possible Tuesday afternoon along the Wind Corridor from Rock Springs 
to Casper. As for snow accumulation probabilistic guidance is 
showing western valleys having a 30-60% chance of at least 1 inch of 
snow. The higher elevations of the Teton, Gros Ventre, Wyoming/Salt 
River, and western Wind River Ranges have a 50-70% of 3 or more 
inches of snow accumulation. Other high elevations such as the 
Absaroka and Bighorn Ranges have a 20-50% of seeing 3 inches. Models 
are trying to show the chance for snow light snowfall across the 
lower elevations of central and northern WY. However, the dynamics 
are not very favorable as mentioned before so chances for any snow 
accumulation at this time look very low. The system moves out by 
Wednesday afternoon leaving behind much colder temperatures. If any 
snow accumulation does occur overnight temperatures may be even 
colder than what is currently forecast. Currently Wednesday nights 
lows look to get into the 20s east of the Divide and teens west of 
the Divide. As mentioned earlier, especially for western valleys if 
snow accumulation does occur these lows could be even colder. There 
remains the potential for another possibly more potent system to 
impact the region by the end of the work week into the weekend. 
However, being so far out and with how volatile the current set up 
is its tough to know what to expect at this time. Long range models 
continue to flip flop with not much consensus at this time. So, stay 
tuned as it is looking like the upcoming workweek may be quite 
eventful for the Cowboy State.
